01.event: visits Rav Kahana's house for a wedding and recites the seven blessings
01.outcome: on later days he recites all blessings only when new faces are present
01.summary: Rav Ashi came to Rav Kahana's house during a wedding. On the first day he recited all seven blessings; afterward he recited them all only when new guests were present, otherwise only two.
01.missing: any response, turn or change; it is a report of his practice
01.reason: A report of what a rabbi did, cited as his practice, with no one responding and nothing following.

02.event: disagree for two and a half years over whether man is better off created
02.outcome: they conclude it would be better not to have been created, but one should examine one's deeds
02.summary: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel argued for two and a half years over whether it is better for man to have been created. They voted and concluded it would be better not, but since he exists he should scrutinize his actions.
02.missing: events beyond debate and a vote
02.reason: Mainly a debate, but a long dispute resolved by a vote is a real event with conflict and resolution; sits between borderline and not, so borderline.

03.actor: a certain man and his heirs
03.event: bequeaths a palm tree to his daughter and dies leaving two half-trees
03.turn: heirs want to give her the two halves
03.outcome: not given in the passage (ruling follows in context)
03.summary: A man willed a palm tree to his daughter, then died leaving only two halves of palm trees shared with partners. The heirs wished to give her the two halves.
03.missing: the resolution; the passage is only the setup of a legal case
03.reason: A real incident (will, death, heirs' dispute) but it serves only to set up a legal ruling, with no further narrated change in the passage.

04.event: visits villages and is asked about eiruv with moist beans
04.outcome: in the study hall he is told Rabbi Yannai's ruling
04.summary: Rabbi Yirmeya went to some villages, where he was asked whether moist beans may be used for an eiruv; he did not know. Back in the study hall he was told Rabbi Yannai permitted it.
04.missing: any event beyond the setting and a question and answer
04.reason: A setting plus a question and answer; under the Shabbat 147a ruling the visit only frames the question and is not enough for a story.

05.event: conducts halitza with a slipper, alone, at night
05.summary: Rabba bar Hiyya performed halitza with a non-leather slipper, as a single judge, at night. Shmuel remarked disparagingly on his reliance on minority opinions.
05.missing: any consequence or change after the act
05.reason: A report of what a rabbi did, cited as legal evidence, followed only by a critical remark; no change follows.

06.event: visits his son-in-law Rav Hisda and places his granddaughter on his lap
06.turn: Rav Hisda objects she may be betrothed; they trade accusations of violating rulings
06.outcome: Rav Aha justifies himself by another statement of Shmuel
06.summary: Rav Aha bar Abba visited Rav Hisda and sat his granddaughter on his lap. Rav Hisda asked whether she might be betrothed; Rav Aha retorted that betrothing a minor violates Rav's ruling, and Rav Hisda countered that holding a woman violates Shmuel's. Rav Aha replied he follows another statement of Shmuel.
06.reason: One real action followed mainly by a legal exchange; mostly speech with something happening, shape 1 borderline.

07.event: send a question to Rabbi Helbo
07.missing: the passage is only the opening of a question; no event beyond sending it
07.reason: Sending a question is a quasi-speech act; the passage contains only that, with no conflict or event.

08.event: comes asking for a tenth of her father's estate
08.turn: her brothers say they would pay her in cash if they could
08.outcome: Ameimar is silent, showing his view
08.summary: Rav Minyumi saw a woman come before Ameimar demanding a tenth of her father's estate. Her brothers said they would buy her out with money if they had it, and Ameimar said nothing, which showed he regarded her as a creditor.
08.missing: any narrated change besides coming before the rabbi
08.reason: A case brought before a rabbi where coming before him is the only event, cited as evidence of his view; nothing changes.

09.actor: a half-slave woman and her master
09.summary: A woman who was half maidservant, half free had her master compelled to emancipate her, and he did. The Gemara then discusses whose view the incident follows.
09.missing: why they forced him; the incident is only sketched and filled in by the discussion
09.reason: A real incident with a change (emancipation), but told in one line as precedent and its cause supplied by the discussion, so only part of a story.

10.event: passes by the door of his father-in-law's house
10.outcome: he was punished because he was suspected with his mother-in-law
10.summary: A man passed by his father-in-law's door and Rav Sheshet had him flogged. The Gemara explains he had been suspected regarding his mother-in-law.
10.missing: the background is supplied by the Gemara, not narrated
10.reason: A real event and an act of punishment, but told only as a one-line precedent inside legal discussion.

11.event: an incident of a forgiven debt
11.turn: Rafram pressures Rav Ashi to rule
11.outcome: Rav Ashi collects the full value of the note
11.summary: In a case of a creditor forgiving a sold debt, Rafram pressed Rav Ashi to rule decisively, and Rav Ashi made the creditor pay the full value of the document.
11.missing: the incident itself is only alluded to
11.reason: An alluded incident with a ruling that is itself an act (collecting payment); only part of a story.

12.missing: the passage discusses a Mishnah incident told earlier; it narrates nothing new
12.reason: The Talmud discussing a story already told to work out the law is legal discussion, not a story.

13.missing: any event beyond a ruling and a citation of a list one rabbi saw
13.reason: A ruling and a scholarly challenge; ordinary Talmudic dialogue with no event or conflict beyond it.

14.event: goes to study with Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua
14.turn: the students gang up on him like roosters and prevent him from learning
14.outcome: he learns only one teaching of the mishna
14.summary: Rabbi went to learn Torah from Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua, but the students banded together against him like the fighting roosters of Beit Bukya and would not let him study. He came away having learned only one thing: Rabbi Eliezer's ruling on the hermaphrodite.
14.reason: An event that happened to a sage, with conflict, causality and an outcome (he learned only one thing); more than a bare report.

15.actor: Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya
15.event: acts in a case according to Rav
15.summary: Rav Yosef of Dabil ruled in practice following Rav, and Shmuel was offended, sarcastically asking whether wisdom was measured out to him in a larger measure. The Gemara uses this to show Rav and Shmuel disagreed.
15.missing: any consequence of Shmuel's anger; the rest is the Gemara's analysis
15.reason: A real act and an emotional reaction, but cited inside legal give-and-take with little development; segment 3 is the Gemara's commentary.

16.event: coerces the wealthy Rav Natan bar Ami
16.outcome: collects four hundred dinars for charity
16.summary: Rava forced Rav Natan bar Ami, a wealthy man, to give to charity and extracted four hundred dinars from him.
16.missing: the occasion and any response; told as a one-line precedent
16.reason: A real coercive act with an outcome, but only a one-line precedent cited for a ruling; part of a story.

17.event: asks for her marriage contract because her husband cannot father children
17.turn: dismissed as not commanded, she argues she needs someone in her old age
17.outcome: Rabbi Ami rules the husband must be forced to divorce her
17.summary: A woman came to Rabbi Ami demanding her ketubah because her husband was infertile. He sent her away, saying she is not commanded to procreate. She asked who would care for her in old age, and he ruled that in such a case the husband is forced.
17.reason: Mainly dialogue before a rabbi ending in a ruling, but there is conflict and the rabbi changes his position; prefer borderline.

18.event: a heretic insults him as a man of thorns
18.turn: he retorts by reading the rest of the verse
18.outcome: he reinterprets the verse as praise
18.summary: A heretic mocked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Hananya, calling Israel thorns from Micah. He called the heretic a fool and showed the verse's other half, explaining that the best of Israel protect it like a thorn hedge.
18.missing: any action beyond the exchange of words
18.reason: Speech only, but a genuine confrontation with a heretic is conflict beyond ordinary scholarly debate, so borderline.

19.missing: any one-time event; it reports habitual practices of Rabbi Yohanan and Rava
19.reason: A custom cited as a rabbi's practice that leads to nothing; a habit with no event following is not a story.

20.event: becomes liable to death by burning at the hands of Heaven
20.turn: the Sages say to leave him
20.outcome: he is spared because he served a great man
20.summary: A student of Rabbi Eliezer had incurred death by burning for his sins, but the Sages said to leave him be, since he had served a great man.
20.missing: what he did and what happened afterward; the incident is only alluded to
20.reason: An incident only alluded to, with a decision that changes his fate; part of a story at most.
